findings.summary: totalCount uses count(*) (all result rows) but filteredCount uses COUNT(DISTINCT test_idx) — mismatched units displayed as 'X of Y results' in the UI
findings.failure_scenario: An eval with 10 test cases and 3 prompts per case produces totalCount=30 (result rows) but filteredCount=10 (distinct test indices). The UI shows '10 of 30 results' even though there are only 10 test cases.

findings.summary: numTests defined as testPassCount + testFailCount, excluding testErrorCount — inflates pass rate, per-test cost, avg tokens, and avg latency in the header
findings.failure_scenario: An eval with 80 pass / 10 fail / 10 error results displays '88.89% passing (80/90 cases)' instead of '80% passing (80/100 cases)', and per-test cost is inflated by dividing total cost by 90 instead of 100.

findings.summary: When filteredResultsCount is 0, pageCount = 0 and maxPageIndex = -1, allowing safeRowPageIndex = -1 and a negative pagination.pageIndex
findings.failure_scenario: URL contains rowId parameter while filters produce zero results. pagination.pageIndex is set to -1, which React Table's manual pagination does not handle — could cause rendering errors or infinite loops.

findings.summary: setEvalId(id) called before fetchEvalData; on fetch failure, evalId is left pointing to the failed eval while table/config may be stale from a previous successful load
findings.failure_scenario: User navigates to eval A (loads correctly), then to eval B (fails/404). Store keeps evalId=B but table/config from eval A. UI shows eval A's data labeled as eval B, and subsequent operations use the wrong evalId.

findings.summary: testCaseMetadataIdx indexes json_extract(metadata, '$') instead of json_extract(test_case, '$.metadata'), and is duplicated by metadataIdx on line 137 — search on test_case.metadata has no index coverage
findings.failure_scenario: Search queries filtering on test_case metadata ('json_extract(test_case, $.metadata) LIKE %...%') get no index assistance, causing full table scans. The two duplicate indexes on json_extract(metadata, '$') waste storage and write overhead.

findings.summary: Header stats read prompt.metrics from server, which are absent for evals created before this PR — old evals display '0.00% passing (0/0 cases)' with zero token/cost/latency stats
findings.failure_scenario: A user views an eval created before the PR deployment. The eval's saved prompts have no metrics object. All header stats show 0 or empty values — '0.00% passing (0/0 cases)', $0.00 cost, 0 tokens, 0ms latency — despite valid results existing.

findings.summary: BAMModerations interface drops the social_bias field and changes structure from {input: {enabled: boolean}} to {input?: boolean} — breaking existing BAM provider moderation configs
findings.failure_scenario: A user has a promptfoo config with BAM provider and moderations: { social_bias: { input: { enabled: true, threshold: 0.7 } } }. After this change, social_bias is silently dropped from the API request, and the nested enabled boolean is no longer parsed correctly, disabling content moderation.

findings.summary: comparisonEvalIds stored in zustand persist middleware survives page reloads — stale eval IDs from deleted evals cause all table requests to fail with 404
findings.failure_scenario: User adds a comparison eval, closes the browser. Days later, that comparison eval has been deleted. On page reload, the stale comparisonEvalIds are sent to the /eval/:id/table endpoint. The server returns 404 for the entire request, and the main eval table also fails to load.

findings.summary: Search debounce increased from 200ms to 1000ms, making search feel 5x slower with server-side processing on top
findings.failure_scenario: User types a search query. Previously debounced at 200ms (near-instant feedback), now debounced at 1000ms (1-second delay) plus network round-trip. Combined with server-side search, total latency exceeds 1 second, degrading UX significantly.

findings.summary: Grader.getResult now unconditionally passes goal instead of conditionally passing newInjectVar for intent plugin — combined with simplified IntentGrader rubric, this changes the evaluated prompt for intent-based red team tests
findings.failure_scenario: An intent-based red team test with pluginId='intent' previously passed the dynamic newInjectVar (the crafted jailbreak prompt) to the grader. Now it passes goal (the high-level intent). Combined with the IntentGrader rubric change removing multi-turn context, the grader evaluates a different input, potentially producing different pass/fail results.
